sections.kicker: Prepared for Ophelia Westgarth by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Your posters look like Ophelia. Your bio looks like every café.
sections.keep: The hand drawn posters for supper club, steak night and pasta night. Nobody else on the street has them.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.

pins.quote: Your neighbourhood café by day, wine bar by night.
pins.what: The bio describes a format, not Ophelia.
pins.why: This is why it looks like everyone else: café by day, wine bar by night is the line half of Melbourne uses.
pins.how: Write the one sentence only Ophelia could say, in the voice of the posters.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: New neighbours file you with every other all day café.

pins.what: Opening hours take the space of a promise.
pins.why: Hours are useful, but they push out any reason to choose you.
pins.how: Move hours to the link and give the bio to the idea.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: The most read words on your profile are a timetable.

pins.area: Three hand drawn posters for supper club, steak night and pasta night
pins.what: The illustrated posters are the most Ophelia thing you own.
pins.why: They already have a hand, a palette and a voice that no neighbour shares.
pins.how: Make that drawing style the identity: signage, menus, bio and site.
pins.label: Your grid
pins.cost: It stays a weekly poster instead of becoming the brand.

sections.intro: You told us Ophelia looks like everyone else and you want it to look like the place you are. I agree with half of that.

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on Ophelia Westgarth's own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
sections.note: A few short questions first, then you pick a time. You can also just reply to the email.

reference: Noma, from another category. Every menu and poster reads like the same hand drew it.
